recipes.name: Homemade Deviled Ham Spread
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch caraway seeds, or to taste

steps.text: Combine ham, mayonnaise, mustard, garlic powder, onion powder, celery salt, black pepper, paprika, hot pepper sauce, and caraway seeds in a large bowl.
Purée ham mixture using an immersion blender or food processor until reaches desired texture. Stir in onion and celery. Refrigerate until chilled before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Deviled Ham Spread
raw_recipe.description: My homemade deviled ham spread recipe with mayo, mustard, hot sauce, onion, celery, spices, and seasonings is perfect for using leftover holiday ham.
raw_recipe.name: Homemade Deviled Ham Spread

review.reviewBody: This was so good. When I was a kid, deviled ham and cream cheese was my very favorite sandwich. The canned stuff is just awful, nutritionally so I made due with good memories. When I found this recipe, I knew I had to try it. I used fat free mayo, a very lean ham and left out the carway seed. I toosed it all into the food processor. I made a sandwich with this and fat free cream cheese... and it was wonderful!

This very good. We both loved it. I used leftover ham. I omitted the celery salt because ham already has plenty of sodium in it. Instead I added 1/2 tsp. of dried celery for flavor. Also, as I was pureeing the ingredients, it seemed a bit dry, so I added about 1/4 cup of chicken broth. Probably won't be buying nearly as much ham spread at the deli counter any more.

Blended the sauce and spices. Used the mini-processor on the celery and onion. Stirred it all with the ham and used the immersion blender. Worked fast with good results. Served with red and yellow bell pepper strips, celery sticks, and Boursin cheese. Nice little dinner. Didn't miss the sweet relish in the usual ham salad.

I increased the amount of ham used by about 1 cup.
tasted a bit bland at first, so I added a teaspoon Worcestershire Sauce, some chopped dill pickles and a teaspoon of cayenne.
Super duper! Put everything into the food processor and whipped into a frenzy! Love this, will put it in my recipe box!

This was perfect for leftovers. I added more mayo and mustard as it was on the dry side. Also added more pepper and hot sauce to suit bf's taste. Used celery seed (half) as the ham was already salty. Left out the caraway seeds. Threw in the celery and onion (red) in the food processor instead of at the end. Came out really good! Thanks for the recipe
I used fresh garlic and added horseradish instead of hot sauce. I believe if I hadn't had to substitute anything it would have been just as good. I will definitely be making this again.
I skipped the caraway seeds and added a heaping tablespoon of pickle relish. Also used a combo of regular and smoked paprika.

Updated to add:
I've made this several times now. I like a bit of sweetness in my ham spread so I put in miracle whip as well as mayonnaise. I put everything in my food processor and whir it all together. This has become my go to recipe for leftover ham.

Original review: I didn't have celery or caraway seeds so I omitted them. The spread still turned out really good and I think this will be my go to recipe for ham salad.

Excellent recipe and so easy. This was so much better than the canned devils Ham and we knew what all of the ingredients that were in it were! Used olive based mayonnaise and added 1/4 teaspoon dried celery and left off the celery salt. Also added 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and 1/4 teaspoon lemon juice. This additions made for a great tasting spread. Will be making it again and again.
This is so far the best recipe I’ve used for deviled ham. Next time I’ll chop the onions and celery in a small processor for smaller pieces. Caraway seeds added a fantastic note. Just a great recipe.

I was delighted with this recipe. I might add that using a cooked ham is not replaced with a Cure 81 style pressed ham which though good, the texture is off but edible for sure. My wife is on a "No Added Salt" diet so I omitted the salts. After the first meal, I ground and added 1/2 teaspoon of Celery Seed. This, in my option added a depth to the flavor. At that time I also added ground red cayenne pepper which again added something to the flavor. I used it with lettuce and tomato on sourdough bread. I put it on saltines, Ritz, Celery and even added to a scrambled egg sandwich . I'll make again right after our next ham Bake!
I did add a green onion, thinly sliced and more finely chopped celery plus instead of mayonnaise, I'd used creamy Caesar salad dressing to make the spread easier to use! I used my food processor.
Made as written and found it to be a fair base, but lacked in flavor.
I did not add onion powder, celery salt or caraway. just added extra celery and onion. I also substituted a tiny amount of wisabi powder since did not have hot sauce.
So tasty and such a good way to use up extra ham. May taste spicy on its own but ointment a sandwich it is perfect.
This recipe turned out better than I thought. I put in a little more pepper sauce because I like spicy food. It gets better when it is a day old. My husband loved it.
Made this with leftover Easter ham and my husband loved it! I did add a little extra mayonnaise to make it more moist.
I don't remember Deviled Ham Spread being spicey, but I'll try it. The rest of the recipe sounds really good. However, I'll probably put some hot sauce in it.
Made for a great sandwich too!
